name: Music-First Voiceover Assembly
use_when: A voiceover-led video needs a clear vibe before the visual pass is complete.
The editor wants to cut some visuals or transitions to music beats.
Music choice will shape pacing, humor, momentum, or production value.
avoid_when: Dialogue timing and story structure are still too unstable.
The project is sensitive, testimony-heavy, or realism-focused and music should be chosen later with restraint.
No licensed or platform-safe track options are available.

timeline_pattern.pattern: voiceover_import -> script_based_trim -> early_music_bed -> volume_under_vo -> asset_layering -> beat_cut_experiments -> later_mix_qc
timeline_pattern.voiceover_rule: Trim the voiceover for flow before letting music dictate timing.
timeline_pattern.music_rule: Add music early only when it clarifies the intended vibe and helps beat-aware decisions.
timeline_pattern.mix_rule: Early music is provisional until the final dialogue clarity and license check pass.

motion.rule: Use beat cuts, zooms, and transition accents only where the music supports the visual or story beat.

sound.rule: Keep music low enough under voiceover during assembly and re-check full mix after SFX and visuals are added.

captions.rule: Do not let music force caption timing that no longer follows the spoken line.

color.rule: Music may influence the visual vibe, but color should still preserve readability and subject detail.

implementation.ffmpeg: Generate rough exports with music bed and voiceover levels for review; use volume automation and loudness checks later.
implementation.remotion: Store voiceoverCut, musicCandidate, cueFrames, beatCutCandidates, and mixStatus separately so the track can change safely.
implementation.blender: Use the early music bed for temporary animation timing only if the track is likely to remain licensed/approved.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Place VO first, add a low music bed, mark beats, and keep track replacement possible.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Import voiceover, trim by script, place licensed/platform-safe music early for vibe, add beat markers, then layer assets and revisit the mix.

common_mistakes: Letting music hide weak voiceover pacing instead of trimming the script.
Cutting to a temp track that cannot be licensed later.
Leaving early music too loud after visual and SFX passes are added.
Forcing every visual cut to the beat when the story needs space.
qc: Is the voiceover understandable before music is added?
Is the early music licensed, platform-safe, or marked temp-only?
Does the music clarify the intended vibe?
Do beat cuts land on meaningful visual or story moments?
Was the final dialogue/music/SFX mix rechecked after the early assembly?
